correctness.rationale: Pure Nash is exactly the pair of weak majority-of-opponents inequalities for every vertex. Mixed parts imply equality of neighboring-one counts; all mixed occupancies are equal. Cases t=0, t=1 and t>=2 are both necessary and sufficient, with admissible integer c. Disjoint exact combinatorial counting yields E_{r,n}. Tripartite r=3 eliminates t=2, allows t=3 only at n even, and gives 6(2^n-1)+1_{2|n} C(n,n/2)^3. Each optimal coloring has cut 2n^2; all-half splits have 3n^2/2. Multiaffinity of cut size proves the 2n^2 global upper bound. Formula, boundary, welfare counts cross-checked by 34 macro and 17 independent labeled enumerations plus 11 direct tripartite cases, using packaged verify.py. Finite tests are auxiliary, not universal proof.

evidence: Deligkas et al. give general optimization/complexity statements for polymatrix games, not enumeration of Nash solutions for complete multipartite graphs in the inspected theorem/appendix material. Lampis studies algorithms on general graphs for minimum stable cuts. Cao–Yang treats an asymmetric maximum-independent-cut regime.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A covering theorem would have to classify and enumerate all pure equilibria of balanced complete r-partite graphs with indifference allowed, or deliver a stronger formula implying those counts and welfare extremes. Complexity and existence results alone are insufficient to imply the present formula.

value.rationale: The natural family of symmetric two-action social anti-coordination games on equal complete multipartite graphs admits an exact all-size Nash classification, polynomial-summand count and nontrivial tripartite parity phase boundary. Even tripartite part sizes create an exponentially dominating inefficient Nash population with exact welfare gap 4/3, while every odd tripartite size has only globally optimal Nash states. These are structural and welfare-relevant effects, not mere computation of an arbitrary instance. No downstream result is assumed.
